call.text: The routing module decides chunk boundaries by measuring cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs and converting this similarity into a boundary probability p_t that ranges from 0 to 1 [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. Specifically, it first projects each encoder output \hat{x}_t to query q_t and key k_t vectors, then computes p_t = ½ (1 − (q_t^⊤ k_{t‑1}) / ‖q_t‖‖k_{t‑1}‖) [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. A hard boundary indicator b_t is set to 1 when p_t ≥ 0.5 and to 0 otherwise, with p_1 defined as 1.0 to ensure the sequence starts with a boundary [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. This mechanism implements the intuition that lower similarity between consecutive vectors signals a contextual or semantic shift, prompting a chunk boundary [HNET:1:c007].
